searchText: Is the EIP bot stuck? https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/3545 Often is. Which is why we are trying to replace it. Merci beaucoup 🙂 In the last EIP IP meeting https://github.com/ethereum-cat-herders/EIPIP/blob/master/All%20EIPIP%20Meetings/Meeting%20031.md Creating a separate ERC repository was discussed, which would effectively remove ERCs from the EIP repository. Similarly, removing EIP 1 from the EIP repository has also been proposed. We’ve been adding these proposals to the WIP “EIP Signal Source Cleanup” document: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1hUpMQh9gA5z3WSDvXKqU_CS6g3Y0hugJZHDYQdKxot8/edit Sam Richards has been making some comments in that document and asking great questions. Specifically, he is asking if we are going to remove EIP 1, do we intend on removing all meta EIPs, providing this link: https://eips.ethereum.org/meta As I indicated, it has been proposed in the last EIP IP meeting that we would create a new ERC repository, as a new separate home for ERC EIPs. It seems to me, if we remove meta EIPs, we would similarly need to create an additional home for Meta EIPs to manage things like EIP 1. Again, more work to find a maintainer of yet another git repository. Sam mentioned that he read somewhere that a goal was to take network upgrades out of the EIP process. Is this true? If so, is this a separate proposal from the separation proposals above? I’m trying to get educated on and collect all the issues around all this. But it seems to me if we want to have a single source of truth for EIPs, what we have now seems ideal to me Everything can be maintained in the same single source of truth repository (far less work). Also, for the people that want things to be separated, the tabs on eips.ethereum.org make this possible. If one only wants core EIPs, without ERCs, they can just select on the core tab, right? Anyway, for those proposing removing ERCs, EIP 1 and such from the EIP repository, does keeping things the way they are make sense? If not, can you guys help me understand where we want to end up with all this? My dream (maybe not realistic, maybe not everyone agrees) is to get Ethereum specced out in a human readable set of markdown files in an eth-specs repository. The change process would be PRs against that, which would me merged to master when a hard fork goes live. This would obviate the need for either Core or Network EIPs and people could just submit spec PRs. I would also like to see the JSON-RPC specs moved into a similar format. That leaves Meta, Informational, and ERCs, which I'm far more ambivalent about. That is a pretty distant future I suspect though, as the act of speccing out all of Ethereum in a human readable form is a non-trivial task. I think this would be good as it would match the eth2 format too Rewrite the yellow paper in python? 😆 This might happen 🙂 ! We can just start with pythereum or whatever it is called. Then we are basically done! If we are doing single source of truth, it must be that, right? Probably a dumb question, due to the fact that I spend most of my time with the Eth 1.0 people. I take it, then, that we do have an Eth 2.0 spec? Where is this and how does this work? Are all problems resolved with that, or is it at least working? Is it more than just the most popular set of source code and the hierarchy that controls that, and if you don't like it, just fork and go someplace else? <https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-specs> thx I do think we should take care to optimize the python spec implementation for readability and not execution efficiency *or* modularity It's a spec, not a client Is there also a separate repository for the python spec implementation? Is this what you guys are talking about? https://pypi.org/project/eth2spec/ That sounds about right. "Stagnant" is not status to be added in the EIP by author or editor. However, it is a state that is achieved by being inactive for a certain period of time and the PR is marked "Stale" by EIP bot. "Withdrawn" is the status that an author / EIP editor can add to the proposal. Probably we can omit the "Stagnant" status from this image. > an additional home for Meta EIPs Meta EIP with "Final" status provides information about Ethereum upgardes. So probably the new home could be eth1.0 spec repo?

excerpts.author: brent.allsop
excerpts.content:
In the last EIP IP meeting https://github.com/ethereum-cat-herders/EIPIP/blob/master/All%20EIPIP%20Meetings/Meeting%20031.md
Creating a separate ERC repository was discussed, which would effectively remove ERCs from the EIP repository.
Similarly, removing EIP 1 from the EIP repository has also been proposed.

We’ve been adding these proposals to the WIP “EIP Signal Source Cleanup” document:
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1hUpMQh9gA5z3WSDvXKqU_CS6g3Y0hugJZHDYQdKxot8/edit

Sam Richards has been making some comments in that document and asking great questions.

Specifically, he is asking if we are going to remove EIP 1, do we intend on removing all meta EIPs, providing this link:
https://eips.ethereum.org/meta

As I indicated, it has been proposed in the last EIP IP meeting that we would create a new ERC repository, as a new separate home for ERC EIPs.

It seems to me, if we remove meta EIPs, we would similarly need to create an additional home for Meta EIPs to manage things like EIP 1.  Again, more work to find a maintainer of yet another git repository.

Sam mentioned that he read somewhere that a goal was to take network upgrades out of the EIP process.  Is this true?  If so, is this a separate proposal from the separation proposals above?

I’m trying to get educated on and collect all the issues around all this.  But it seems to me if we want to have a single source of truth for EIPs, what we have now seems ideal to me  Everything can be maintained in the same single source of truth repository  (far less work).
Also, for the people that want things to be separated, the tabs on eips.ethereum.org make this possible.  If one only wants core EIPs, without ERCs, they can just select on the core tab, right?

Anyway, for those proposing removing ERCs, EIP 1 and such from the EIP repository, does keeping things the way they are make sense?  If not, can you guys help me understand where we want to end up with all this?
